sheet.method: Learn then Test on the learned prefix score (fitted on the fit + policy-grid items, one row per word prefix), loss = wrong prefix commit, exact binomial p-values, fixed-sequence grid 1.00 -> 0.00 step 0.01, on the LTT items only

controls.name: shuffled
controls.description: calibration frames in a random time order

controls.name: user
controls.description: your decoder output on null input (null_inputs)

assumptions: Exchangeable data: the calibration utterances and the live utterances come from the same distribution (same user, device, decoder, task and session type). Use a random sample, not a hand-picked one.
The decoder, its weights, the vocabulary and the decode settings do not change after calibration.
The true texts are right, and they use the same text normalisation as the decoder output (the wrapper joins runs of spaces and strips the ends; nothing else).
Each utterance is decided once (no repeats), and the calibration items were used for nothing else.
not_guaranteed: Any single utterance: the bound is on the rate over many utterances.
A bound per session, per user or per sentence type: the bound is on the mix of the calibration data.
Data that differ from the calibration data (a new day, a new electrode position, a new user, drift).
The error rate among commits (precision): with few commits it can be high.
The quality of offered choices, or how often the guard commits (it may commit rarely or never).
Correctness of the text that the guard withholds or offers.
Any medical or legal claim. Fidetype is research software, not a medical device.
warnings: frame temperature not fitted (1.0): with your own decode_fn, pass stream_texts= (the truth in the decoder's token space) to fit it. The guarantee does not depend on it.

confidence.model: logistic regression, L2 on standardised features, features clipped to the fit range, sign-constrained weights (backward elimination)
confidence.risk: wrong-prefix-commit: the committed words are not the first words of the true text (a complete prefix, i.e. the whole top-1 text, is wrong unless it equals the true text); rate over all utterances
